items.item: A quartz oscillator drifts continuously; NTP's correction is a continuous process against a continuously moving target, not a one-time fix.

at.step: Reveal: a crystal drifts continuously, and NTP's own fix has its own error bar

items.item: NTP's offset formula assumes a symmetric network path; an asymmetric path biases the offset estimate without the protocol being able to detect it from the four timestamps alone.
A leap second handled by smearing on one clock and stepping on another produces a full day of disagreement between two equally correct clocks, not a one-second blip.

at.step: Reveal: a leap second, smeared by one clock and stepped by another

items.item: A wall clock can jump (forward or back) when corrected; a monotonic clock never jumps but is meaningless across machines; a paused process can hold either stale for an unbounded time.

at.step: Reveal: wall clock, monotonic clock, and the pause neither survives

items.item: A bounded-error clock returns an interval (earliest, latest) instead of a point, so two overlapping intervals are an honest, explicit signal that two events cannot be ordered.

at.step: Reveal: an honest interval beats a confident, wrong point

items.item: A lease is only safe once its length exceeds the maximum clock skew the two parties could ever disagree by, not the skew that is merely typical.

at.step: Prove it: is a lease sized to last month's typical clock skew safe?
